prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map places the tabletop in front of the wearer at roughly 0.4–1.0 m, with the wearer’s hands and forearms at the bottom nearest the camera, about 0.2–0.5 m away; two people sit across the table, approximately 1–1.5 m from the wearer and about 0.5–1 m from each other. Tabletop books, bowls, cups and glasses lie below and in front of those people, mostly within the wearer’s reach near the front edge or within the opposite diners’ reach farther back. Across the five frames, a foreground hand rises near the centre in frame 3, then an arm from the person on the right extends diagonally toward the camera and becomes much nearer in frames 4–5, partially occluding the table. Brightness makes these near/far layers clearer than the dark RGB, but metric distances are only rough: object boundaries merge, the people’s torsos blend with the background, and the map cannot reliably establish gaze direction or distinguish lateral camera motion from true approach.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map separates two people seated side by side across the table and, in frame 1, also marks a large partly visible foreground person region belonging to the camera-wearer side; the opposite people are roughly 1–1.5 m from the camera and within about 0.5–1 m of each other. It localizes the dining table below them and identifies books, bowls, cups and a wine glass distributed from left to right, clarifying overlaps that are difficult to distinguish in the dark RGB; the nearest tableware is about 0.4–0.7 m from the wearer, while items by the opposite edge are about 0.8–1.2 m away. Frames 3–5 show the right-hand person’s arm crossing downward and toward the foreground, covering part of the table and bringing the hand into the wearer’s arm-reach zone, while the two seated bodies remain at broadly similar depth and shift laterally with the viewpoint. The masks do not establish facing or gaze reliably, omit people in frame 2, fragment or mislabel several small objects, and sometimes absorb arms, table areas and occluded boundaries into incorrect instances.
descriptions.pose: The pose map exposes articulated limbs and hands that nearly disappear in the RGB: frame 1 shows an upper-body/arm skeleton across the far-left upper area and a separate foreground hand near the lower left, while frames 4–5 show hand keypoints near the two people across the table. In frame 4, a long arm skeleton runs from the upper-right diner diagonally toward the table centre and nearer camera space, indicating extension from roughly 1–1.5 m away to a hand perhaps 0.5–0.8 m from the wearer; by frame 5 the hand cluster remains visible but the connecting arm is lost. The hand positions show reach relative to the tabletop and nearby cups or bowls more clearly than RGB, but sparse head and torso landmarks prevent a dependable judgment of which way either person faces or whether either looks at the wearer. Missing skeletons in frames 2–3, disconnected hand/body tracks, and the disappearance of the extended limb in frame 5 make apparent approach, retreat and turning unreliable, especially where bodies are cropped or occluded by the table and one another.
